A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Matching relocated content supports a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular-prediction and NLP experiments, including performance correlations, hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, and dimension-based comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds a hyperparameter-transfer evaluation in Appendix D.2 and Table 2.

M1.justification: The W2SG training procedures, representation-extraction heuristics, and principal-kernel prediction metrics remain unchanged. The new hyperparameter-transfer experiment evaluates the existing approach.

E1.justification: Both versions use GuacaMol pretraining and the same eight downstream datasets: ESOL, FreeSolv, Lipop, Justice, Commonsense, SciQ, Amazon Polarity, and Cosmos QA. The added model-split experiment uses existing Justice and Commonsense coverage.

E2.justification: The weak and strong model rosters remain unchanged, as do the activation-map dimension and principal-representation dimension comparators in Figures 5 and 11. Table 2 introduces no additional comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 adds a protocol that randomly divides weak models equally, selects hyperparameters on one half, and evaluates correlation on the other. This supplements the existing evaluations; their training settings, metrics, and hyperparameter grids remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 already contains hyperparameter sensitivity sweeps in Figures 6–7. v3 adds a focused analysis testing whether hyperparameters selected using some weak models transfer to held-out models, reported in Table 2.

E5.justification: The added transfer experiment explicitly repeats random model splitting 20 times and reports mean correlations with standard deviations. This introduces uncertainty reporting over model splits without changing the reporting of existing experiments.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports held-out-model Spearman correlations of 0.885 ± 0.16 for Justice and 0.67 ± 0.20 for Commonsense. Existing numerical results and plotted findings in Figures 2–11 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definition 3.3(b) restores missing summations in both representation–label concentration expressions, correcting the empirical terms to sample averages. The theorem statements, derivations, and proofs in Appendices A–C otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same principal-kernel characterization, explanation of benign overfitting, and label-agnostic performance-prediction claims. The additional validation does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 adds discussion connecting the isotropy condition to high-dimensional noise in neural networks. Appendix D.2 interprets the new results as supporting transferable hyperparameters and explicitly discusses using labeled data for tuning while keeping metric computation label-free.

D1.justification: Model identifiers, optimizers, learning rates, training budgets, hyperparameter grids, and codebase references remain unchanged. The four shared hyperparameters explained in v3 Section 5.2 were already documented in v1 Appendix D.2; the new evaluation design is covered under E3 and E5.

R1.justification: A new remark after Theorem 4.1 sharpens the comparison with Wu and Sahai (2024), contrasting their specified representation assumptions with this paper's general error-propagation criterion. The bibliography and broader related-work discussion remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Local revisions rename Section 3.3 from 'Assumption' to 'Setting', expand explanatory remarks, repeat the existing hyperparameter-sharing explanation in the main text, and update an author affiliation. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 2 and redistributes existing figures across pages, including moving Figure 4 and placing Figure 11 on a separate final page. Existing graphics, axes, legends, and Table 1 retain their content.

improvement.justification: The held-out-model experiment in Appendix D.2 and Table 2 strengthens evidence that hyperparameter choices transfer beyond the models used for selection, with uncertainty across 20 splits. Correcting Definition 3.3(b) also improves mathematical precision. These are useful but limited gains: transfer is tested on only two embedding-model tasks, with standard deviations of 0.16 and 0.20, while the main theory and original results remain unchanged.
